title: Lease-Free Reservation & Echo Suppression for Duplicate-Usage Prevention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: At-least-once delivery from edge gateways and flaky mobile/SDK clients causes duplicated ingest events that lead to transient over-billing and noisy quota enforcement. Existing approaches in the codebase largely rely on client-side leases, long-lived ack windows, or per-customer session anchors, which add operational state, lockstep client upgrades, or expensive coordination for high-throughput customers.

Goal: Design a lightweight, lease-free server-side pattern that suppresses short-term duplicate echoes at the edge while preserving eventual strong accounting correctness and low-latency paths for small requests. The solution should: 1) avoid per-request long-lived locks on revenue paths, 2) work across multi-region edge relays, 3) degrade gracefully under partition, and 4) provide clear reconciliation signals for billing correctness audits.
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce an ephemeral Echo-Suppression Token (EST) pattern: clients compute a compact 64-bit request fingerprint (client-signed), attach it as EST to requests. Edge relays maintain a small, time-decayed in-memory probabilistic filter (count-min + time-decay) per-edge-region to suppress immediate echoes for a short window (e.g., 60s). Servers do a low-cost canonicalization and append the fingerprint to the ingest stream. Downstream metering uses a final deterministic commit step: a batched commit ledger that deduplicates by canonical fingerprint before final billing. This creates a two-tier defense: fast suppression at ingress plus eventual dedupe in billing finalizer. No per-request reservations or leased tokens are required.
tradeoffs_and_risks: False positives at edge: probabilistic filters may drop a distinct retry if collision occurs; choose parameters to keep FP < 1e-6 for normal QPS ranges.
Delayed reconciliation: short suppression window means retries beyond window can still appear duplicated and rely on final reconciliation. This could surface briefly in quotas and dashboards.
Client upgrades: requires SDKs/clients to emit canonical fingerprints; fallback heuristic will be used for older clients which increases backend reconciliation load.

Multi-region duplicates: identical requests arriving in different regions create transient duplicate risk; canonicalization + final dedupe mitigates billing impact but increases reconciliation complexity.
Monitoring complexity: new metrics required to track suppression rate, FP rate, and reconciliation adjustments to billing.
Regulatory/audit: must keep immutable logs and allow deterministic replay during audits to explain reconciliations.
acceptance_criteria: Edge suppression reduces immediate duplicate ingestion rate by >= 90% for live SDK tests (same-client retries within 60s)
Billing finalizer deduplicates to < 0.001% net duplicate charge after a 24h reconciliation window on synthetic workloads
No per-request leasing services introduced; CPU/memory overhead on edge relays remains < 5% at 99th percentile load
Client SDKs optionally emit EST; servers accept EST and fall back deterministically for legacy clients
Dashboard surfaces suppressed-count, collision-count, and reconciliation-adjustments with alerting thresholds
implementation_plan: Design: formalize EST format (64-bit fingerprint + client signature metadata) and canonicalization rules (what constitutes identical requests)
Edge: implement per-node time-decayed count-min filter module with exportable metrics; integrate suppression hook that returns rapid 409-suppressed for duplicates when appropriate
API: accept EST header and validate signature for clients that opt-in; add deterministic request canonicalizer in ingestion path
Metering: extend billing finalizer to use fingerprint dedupe stage during batch finalize; store canonical fingerprints in append-only commit ledger for 30 days
Client: release SDK patch that emits EST derived from request payload + client nonce; provide server-side fallback docs
Testing: run canary tests with mobile SDK, slow networks, and multi-region replay scenarios
Rollout: staged rollout — start with non-billing traffic flag, then opt-in customers, then global default with reconciliation monitoring
rollout_plan: Week 1: feature branch + unit tests; deploy edge module behind flag in staging
Week 2: internal canary for Redwood engineers + selected beta customers; monitor suppression and collisions
Week 3: enable EST acceptance for all traffic (no suppression) to collect telemetry and fingerprint prevalence
Week 4: enable suppression edge-side for 10% of production regions; enable billing-finalizer dedupe in dry-run mode
Week 5: expand suppression to 50% and enable reconciliation adjustments to billing reports (non-invoice) for validation
Week 6: full rollout and deprecation plan for long-lived leasing mechanisms once steady-state metrics confirm targets
monitoring_and_metrics: fingerprint_coverage_percent (fraction of incoming traffic with valid EST)
comments: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — microbenchmarks show count-min decay filter < 2MB/node for 60s window at 20k RPS.
2026-03-04: PM review (Miguel Santos) — requested explicit fallback behavior for legacy clients and an opt-out for high-sensitivity customers.
2026-03-05: Design review — added requirement for append-only commit ledger retention (30 days) for audits.
2026-03-07: Security review kickoff — flagged client signature format for crypto review; added to security_review_required.
2026-03-09: QA reported rare collision on sampled synthetic tests; tuned count-min parameters and added collision metric.
2026-03-10: Engineering lead (Priya Rao) approved go/no-go for staging canary; staging rollout scheduled for 2026-03-15.
